subject.title: feat: nameplate attention --wait blocks until the human acknowledges

question: Should `nameplate attention --wait` permanently map click to exit 0, app-driven dismissal to exit 3, and both timeout and supersession to exit 4?
rationale: The implementation and proof support this coherent mapping, but scripts will depend on it after release and source inspection cannot choose among other reasonable public contracts.

options.title: Approve current mapping
options.body: Adopt the demonstrated 0/3/4 contract so agents can distinguish human acknowledgment from app-driven or no-ack completion without extra complexity.

options.title: Split lifecycle outcomes
options.body: Assign separate codes to forced dismissal, supersession, and timeout before the first release if scripts need finer branching.

recommendation.title: Approve current mapping
recommendation.body: Adopt the demonstrated 0/3/4 contract so agents can distinguish human acknowledgment from app-driven or no-ack completion without extra complexity.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and most heavily maintained the attention CLI and lifecycle behavior.
